project: MCP Operational Tools — Dev Server, Sync, Build Subprocess Control
description: Extend tools/overview-mcp with 7 new subprocess-management tools (overview.dev_server.{start,stop,status,logs}, overview.build, overview.sync.now, overview.sync.watch_status) backed by a shared ProcessManager class with ring-buffered logs, single-flight enforcement, Vite ready-signal parsing, and Windows tree-kill shutdown. Also exports a canonical readLockStatus helper from scripts/lib/sync-lock.mjs and adds a parseable stdout summary line to scripts/sync-ralph-state.mjs:runOneShot.

planReviewContext.description: The Vite ready regex `^\s*Local:\s+(\S+)` would not match Vite's arrow-prefixed banner (`  ➜  Local:   http://127.0.0.1:5173/`). Resolved: use one canonical predicate that strips CSI ANSI escapes then matches /Local:\s+(https?:\S+)/ anywhere in the line; assert both arrow-prefixed and plain banners in tests.
planReviewContext.suggestedFix: Strip CSI ANSI escapes with /\x1b\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]/g, then match /Local:\s+(https?:\S+)/ anywhere in the line. Check both stdout and stderr.

planReviewContext.description: Double-start race: when AlreadyRunning is caught, url/pid/startedAt are undefined on the existing handle until 'spawn' fires. Resolved: each ManagedProcess exposes readyPromise; AlreadyRunning callers await it before returning { alreadyRunning: true, url, pid, startedAt }.
planReviewContext.suggestedFix: Add readyPromise: Promise<{url,pid,startedAt}> to ManagedProcess; dev_server.start awaits it on AlreadyRunning.

planReviewContext.description: scripts/lib/sync-lock.d.mts must declare the new readLockStatus export (plus parseLockMetadata, isLockHolderAlive) so overview-mcp NodeNext resolution typechecks. Resolved: .d.mts added to the modify list with matching signatures.
planReviewContext.suggestedFix: Declare readLockStatus(lockPath, opts?) plus parseLockMetadata and isLockHolderAlive in sync-lock.d.mts.

planReviewContext.description: overview.build and overview.sync.now children were originally untracked, so stopAll() would orphan them on SIGTERM. Resolved: both spawn through ProcessManager with reserved names ('build', 'sync-now') and disposeOnExit:true; in-flight transients are included in stopAll().
planReviewContext.suggestedFix: Track 'build' and 'sync-now' as transient ProcessManager entries while running; remove from Map only on exit; ensure stopAll covers them.

planReviewContext.description: Sync summary line referenced `matched`/`unmatched` bindings that do not exist in runOneShot. Resolved: derive matched=Object.keys(state.byTaskId??{}).length, unmatched=(state.unmatched??[]).length, durationMs=Date.now()-startTime (startTime captured at top of runOneShot).
planReviewContext.suggestedFix: Capture startTime at top of runOneShot; derive matched/unmatched from state.byTaskId and state.unmatched; emit single stdout line after sidecar write.

planReviewContext.description: Adding processManager as a required ServerContext field breaks existing makeContext() and any direct ServerContext literals. Resolved: helpers.ts is in the modify list; audit and update all direct context literals (get-transcript.test.ts, list-crew-sessions.test.ts, set-override.test.ts) atomically.
planReviewContext.suggestedFix: Update makeContext() to construct a ProcessManager (optionally injectable). Update every direct ServerContext literal to include the new field.

planReviewContext.description: Start-failure cleanup was missing — a timed-out or pre-ready-exit child would leave a stale 'dev-server' handle. Resolved: wrap spawn+onReady in try/catch; on failure call manager.stop('dev-server', { remove: true }) and return { ok:false, error, lastLogLines }. AC covers failed-start-then-retry.
planReviewContext.suggestedFix: On startup failure, stop and remove the registered dev-server handle so subsequent start can spawn fresh.

planReviewContext.description: On Windows with shell:true the tracked PID may be the shell wrapper, not Vite/Node — killing only that PID would not satisfy the no-orphan AC. Resolved: tree-kill is a v1 runtime dependency; ProcessManager.stop() uses it on Windows for SIGTERM and SIGKILL escalation.
planReviewContext.suggestedFix: Add tree-kill as runtime dependency; use it on win32 for both SIGTERM and SIGKILL escalation in ProcessManager.stop().

planReviewContext.description: No-orphan AC was insufficient — checking a single stored pid does not prove descendants are gone. Resolved: Verification L now captures dev-server pid + port-5173 listener pid before SIGTERM, asserts both are gone afterward, and verifies port 5173 is no longer listening.
planReviewContext.suggestedFix: Capture pid + port listener pid before SIGTERM; assert both gone and port 5173 closed after MCP exits.

planReviewContext.description: sync-lock.mjs refactor burden was implicit. Resolved: modify list now enumerates extract parseLockMetadata, extract/export isLockHolderAlive, implement readLockStatus by composing fs.stat + the helpers; same-module unit tests cover each helper.
planReviewContext.suggestedFix: Extract parseLockMetadata and isLockHolderAlive as exported helpers; implement readLockStatus on top; add unit tests for each.

planReviewContext.description: Ambiguous test location for the sync summary line. Resolved: canonical test is tools/overview-mcp/src/__tests__/sync-now.test.ts spawning the real script in a tmp repo through the MCP tool path; no scripts/__tests__/ fallback.
planReviewContext.suggestedFix: Place the summary-line integration test at tools/overview-mcp/src/__tests__/sync-now.test.ts.

planReviewContext.description: Decomposition prose contradicted itself on parallel vs serial. Resolved: execution_mode is REQUIRED serial for cluster mcp-ops-tools (US-004..US-007) because all four edit server.ts, context.ts, schemas.ts, stdio-tools-list.test.ts, and README.md.
planReviewContext.suggestedFix: Run US-004 through US-007 strictly serially to avoid merge conflicts on the five shared files.

userStories.title: ProcessManager foundation
userStories.description: As an MCP server author, I want a single ProcessManager class that spawns, tracks, ring-buffers, and stops child processes, so each new operational tool can share one lifecycle implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: tools/overview-mcp/src/process-manager.ts exports a ProcessManager class with spawn, stop, status, logs, stopAll, plus ManagedProcess.onReady (checks both stdout and stderr ring buffers).
ProcessManager.spawn registers the ManagedProcess record in its Map with status='starting' BEFORE calling child_process.spawn, closing the double-start race window.

Each ManagedProcess carries a readyPromise: Promise<{ url, pid, startedAt }> that resolves when the first onReady callback fires; callers receiving AlreadyRunning await this promise before constructing their response.
Transient single-flight names ('build', 'sync-now') are tracked while running and auto-removed on 'exit'; in-flight transients ARE included in stopAll().
Children spawn with stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'] and { shell: true }; tests assert the parent's stdout stays clean (no JSON-RPC pollution).
On Windows, stop() uses tree-kill for both SIGTERM and SIGKILL escalation, killing the whole child process tree rather than just the shell wrapper PID.
Ring buffer is capped at 1000 lines per stream; CRLF is normalized to LF before splitting.

tools/overview-mcp/src/__tests__/process-manager.test.ts covers: spawn → logs, onReady (stdout AND stderr), stop (graceful + SIGKILL escalation), stopAll on long-lived + transient mix, already-running guard, double-start race ordering, stop-while-starting, ring-buffer overflow drops oldest, CRLF normalization, stdio isolation.
Typecheck passes for @codexu/overview-mcp.
pnpm --filter @codexu/overview-mcp test passes.
userStories.notes: Estimated complexity: large. Foundational story — pure library, no MCP integration. Must register the ManagedProcess record (including readyPromise) BEFORE calling child_process.spawn to close the double-start race.

userStories.title: sync-lock helper exports
userStories.description: As sync-watch-status.ts and the future MCP toolset, I want a single canonical readLockStatus(lockPath) helper exported from scripts/lib/sync-lock.mjs (plus its building blocks), so lock semantics never drift between watcher and MCP.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/lib/sync-lock.mjs exports parseLockMetadata(buffer), isLockHolderAlive(pid), and readLockStatus(lockPath, opts?).

readLockStatus returns { state: 'missing' } | { state: 'active', pid, process, startedAt, mtime: Date } | { state: 'stale', pid?, process?, startedAt?, mtime?: Date }. Unparseable JSON triggers one 50ms retry before classifying as stale.
When mtime is older than staleAfterMs (default DEFAULT_STALE_AFTER_MS = 60_000) BUT isLockHolderAlive(pid) === true, the result is 'active' (trust PID over mtime).
scripts/lib/sync-lock.d.mts declares the new exports with the documented type shapes so TypeScript consumers (overview-mcp NodeNext resolution) typecheck cleanly.

scripts/lib/sync-lock.test.mjs (or the equivalent existing test file location) covers each helper: parse success/failure, alive PID, dead PID, active mtime, stale mtime + dead PID, stale mtime + alive PID, missing file, unparseable + retry.
No behavior change to existing acquireLock / releaseLock callers.
Typecheck and tests pass for @codexu/overview-mcp (verifies the .d.mts edit).
userStories.notes: Estimated complexity: medium. Refactor extracts parseLockMetadata and isLockHolderAlive as exported helpers, then composes them into readLockStatus. Existing acquireLock / releaseLock must keep their current behavior.

userStories.title: overview.sync.now and overview.sync.watch_status
userStories.description: As an agent, I want overview.sync.now to run the one-shot sync and overview.sync.watch_status to inspect the lock file holder, so I can drive and observe the sync pipeline from MCP.
acceptanceCriteria: tools/overview-mcp/src/tools/sync-now.ts registers overview.sync.now and spawns node scripts/sync-ralph-state.mjs through ProcessManager.spawn({ name: 'sync-now', oneShot: true }). Concurrent calls receive AlreadyRunning → returns { ok: false, error: 'sync already in progress' }.
On exit code 0, the tool parses the stdout summary line and returns { ok: true, summary: { tasksMatched, unmatchedCount, durationMs } }.

userStories.title: Shutdown wiring + README + downstream cascade
userStories.description: As the MCP server, I want ProcessManager.stopAll() invoked inside the existing shutdown() so all spawned children (long-lived and transient) die when SIGTERM arrives. Documentation must reflect the new operational surface, and downstream plans/INDEX references must be refreshed.
acceptanceCriteria: tools/overview-mcp/src/index.ts shutdown() awaits context.processManager.stopAll() between snapshotReader.close() and server.close(), inside a try/catch that logs to stderr so a hung child cannot block the rest of shutdown.
No new SIGTERM/SIGINT/exit handlers are added. The existing handlers (Plan 09) are extended in place.

src/__tests__/shutdown.test.ts (fast) uses real node -e 'setInterval(() => {}, 1000)' children to verify ProcessManager.stopAll() kills BOTH long-lived ('dev-server') and transient ('build', 'sync-now') registered entries within the SIGTERM + SIGKILL window.

src/__tests__/shutdown-vite.test.ts (or describe.skipIf(!process.env.OVERVIEW_MCP_REAL_VITE) block) covers the real-Vite Windows orphan check from verification step L — runnable manually but skipped in CI to avoid flakiness.

tools/overview-mcp/README.md documents the 7 new tools (one section per tool with input/output schema), the lifecycle constraint (children die with MCP), the build single-flight rejection, the ring-buffer cap, the tree-kill Windows dependency, and the dev-server stdio isolation guarantee.
tools/overview-mcp/package.json declares tree-kill as a runtime dependency (or devDependency if only used in tests — the plan uses it in ProcessManager.stop(), so runtime).

Cascade audit: plans/ralph-pipeline-INDEX.md's 'Source-of-truth modules' table and DAG diagram are updated for the new files: tools/overview-mcp/src/process-manager.ts, the 7 new tool files, the new test files, and the modifications to scripts/lib/sync-lock.mjs + scripts/sync-ralph-state.mjs. Plans 02 and 09 are reviewed for any references that drifted (file paths, type signatures, export names, behavior contracts) and updated atomically in the final implementation commit. The commit message lists each diff (file, lines, change) so reviewers can verify the cascade.
All 17 tools are listed in the stdio smoke test by exact set equality.
Final typecheck + test run passes; pnpm overview-mcp:install (and equivalent CI scripts) continue to succeed.
